review.tagline: C/C++ port of OpenAI Whisper for local speech-to-text transcription
review.summary: whisper.cpp runs OpenAI's Whisper speech recognition models in plain C/C++ on top of the ggml library, with a C-style API in whisper.h and a whisper-cli example for transcribing 16-bit WAV files. It runs on CPU or can offload to Metal, Core ML, CUDA, Vulkan, ROCm, OpenVINO, Ascend CANN, Moore Threads MUSA and AMD Ryzen AI NPUs. It supports integer quantization and voice activity detection, and builds for desktop, mobile, WebAssembly and Docker.
review.audience: Developers embedding offline speech-to-text in apps, servers or devices
strengths: No dependencies in core; zero memory allocations at runtime
Wide backend coverage: Metal, Core ML, CUDA, Vulkan, ROCm, OpenVINO, CANN, MUSA, NPU
Runs on iOS, Android, WebAssembly, Raspberry Pi, and Java bindings exist
Q5_0-style integer quantization shrinks models; base model needs about 388 MB RAM
weaknesses: whisper-cli accepts only 16-bit WAV unless built with optional FFmpeg support
Core ML, OpenVINO and VitisAI encoders need a separate Python conversion step
Models must be in ggml format; downloaded via script, not bundled
Library and CLI only; no built-in web UI or multi-user features
needs: Needs CMake, ffmpeg (optional), CUDA / ROCm / Vulkan / OpenVINO (optional backends)
Models: Whisper ggml (tiny, base, small, medium, large-v1/v2/v3, large-v3-turbo), Quantized ggml (e.g. q5_0)
